funFact: Despite its huge body, a Stegosaurus had a brain that was only the size of a walnut.
Triceratops had a massive skull that could grow up to 8 feet long, which is a third of its entire body length.
Tyrannosaurus rex had the strongest bite of any land animal that ever lived, enough to crush a car.
The biggest land dinosaur was Argentinosaurus, which grew up to 130 feet long and weighed as much as 15 elephants.
Velociraptors were not the giant monsters shown in movies; they were actually about the size of a turkey and had feathers.
The Ankylosaurus had a heavy, bony club at the end of its tail that it used to smash predators.
Parasaurolophus had a long tube-like crest on its head that it used like a trumpet to make loud sounds.
The flying reptiles you see in dinosaur books, like Pterodactyls, are called pterosaurs and are not actually dinosaurs.
Plant-eating dinosaurs swallowed small stones called gastroliths to help grind up tough leaves in their stomachs.
Brachiosaurus had front legs that were longer than its back legs, which helped it reach high tree branches.
Spinosaurus was the longest meat-eating dinosaur and spent most of its time swimming and hunting for fish.
Many meat-eating dinosaurs had feathers to stay warm, even though they could not fly.
The first dinosaur fossil ever officially named was the Megalosaurus back in the year 1824.
Dinosaurs lived on every single continent on Earth, including Antarctica, which used to be warm and covered in forests.
Compsognathus was a meat-eating dinosaur about the size of a chicken that could run incredibly fast.
Many plant-eating dinosaurs lived in massive herds for protection, just like today's elephants and zebras.
The word dinosaur means "terrible lizard," but they were actually reptiles, not lizards.
Scientists have discovered and named more than 1,000 different species of dinosaurs.
Dinosaur eggs came in many shapes, but the absolute biggest ones were only about the size of a basketball.
Dinosaur bones are not actual bones anymore; they turned into stone fossils over millions of years.
The Therizinosaurus had giant, scary claws that were over 3 feet long, but it used them to scrape up plants to eat.
A massive asteroid hitting Earth near Mexico 66 million years ago is what caused the dinosaurs to go extinct.
Dinosaurs ruled the Earth for about 165 million years, which is much longer than humans have been here.
Modern birds are actually living dinosaurs, directly evolved from a group of two-legged meat-eaters called theropods.
Some dinosaurs like Maiasaura were excellent parents, building nests and taking care of their babies until they grew up.
The smallest known adult dinosaur was Microraptor, which was only about the size of a crow.
Giant swimming sea monsters like Mosasaurus and Plesiosaurus are also not classified as dinosaurs.
Scientists who dig up and study dinosaur fossils are called paleontologists.
The smartest dinosaurs were likely small meat-eaters like Troodon, which had big brains relative to their body size.
Dinosaur poop that has turned into stone over millions of years is called a coprolite.
Plesiosaurus swam using four flipper-like limbs instead of a tail, more like a sea turtle than a fish.
Liopleurodon had a short neck and a huge head, and it hunted other sea creatures in the deep ocean.
Ichthyosaurus looked a lot like a modern dolphin, even though the two are not related at all.
Pterodactylus was one of the very first flying reptiles ever found, with wings made of skin stretched to its long fourth finger.
